title: Unsoundness in Unsafe Memory Operations
platform_conditions: Any Rust toolchain (stable/nightly); unsafe blocks bypass the borrow checker on every target and optimization level
security_mechanism: Rust's safety guarantees are a contract the programmer must uphold inside every unsafe block: slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len) builds a &[T] valid only if ptr points to len live, initialized, aligned elements for the slice's whole lifetime. A length taken from a protocol header or peer makes the contract attacker-controlled, so the resulting slice lets safe code — which the compiler assumes cannot access invalid memory — read or write far past the real allocation. The same holds for transmute (reinterpreting bytes as a different type, breaking size or layout invariants), MaybeUninit::assume_init (asserting initialization that never happened), get_unchecked (asserting a bound that was never checked), and Vec::set_len (asserting elements exist that were never constructed). Because the type system now believes the lie, the optimizer may elide the real bounds checks that would have caught the access.

source_sink_clues.source: Lengths, pointers, and layout assumptions derived from peer data: wire-format length prefixes, FFI-returned pointers and counts, descriptor tables.
source_sink_clues.sink: unsafe { slice::from_raw_parts / from_raw_parts_mut } with an external length; transmute; MaybeUninit::assume_init; get_unchecked(_mut); Vec::set_len

tracking_guards: Check that the length/pointer is validated against a real bound (allocation size, protocol maximum) BEFORE entering the unsafe block, that the provenance of the pointer is documented and within-lifetime, and that initialization claims (assume_init, set_len) are backed by writes that already happened; flag any unsafe block whose inputs include unvalidated external values.
not_candidate_when: The unsafe block's length is clamped to the real allocation before entry and the bound is enforced in safe code, the pointer/length come from a checked internal invariant established at construction, or the block is covered by a reviewed abstraction whose safe API validates every input (and the external input never reaches the unsafe inputs).
synthetic_safe_example: if external_len <= max_len { unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, external_len) }; }
public_references: CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/119.html
